answer: An agent economy can require every account to post a refundable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independently checked tasks reveal fraud or duplicate identities coordinating to claim rewards. Honest agents recover their stake, so the rule need not exclude newcomers; a sybil operator, however, must lock capital for each identity and risks losing it across many accounts. Making identities feel as distinct as marble, ember, and shale does not help: the cost scales with the number of identities, not their names.
